type: primary-source constraints; no F135 calibration claimed

sources.title: Experimental and numerical study of chemiluminescent species in low-pressure flames
sources.reviewed: Sections 2, 4, 7 and Table 5; full author manuscript
sources.domain: Primarily methane/oxygen/argon and methane/hydrogen/oxygen/argon premixed flames at 0.05 bar; no soot model.
sources.supports: Separate production and radiative/collisional loss; precursor sensitivity; Table 5 radiative rates CH(A) 1.86e6/s and C2(d) 1e7/s.
sources.doesNotSupport: A fuel-to-visible efficiency, equal CH/C2 powers, F135 populations or external reaction distribution.
sources.caution: Table 5 C2 collider list does not establish nitrogen quenching. The manuscript also gives different band-averaged coefficients for experimental intensity conversion; those must not be interchanged with total electronic-state loss.

sources.title: Chemiluminescence (Kathrotia 2012)
sources.supports: The institute offers the excited-species submechanism alone and with C1-C4 chemistry.
sources.doesNotSupport: Validated kerosene/F135 chemistry from bulk fuel flow alone.
sources.implementationStatus: Not downloaded, installed or incorporated during this audit.

sources.title: Cross sections for quenching of CH A2Delta, v=0, by N2 and H2O from 1740 to 2160 K
sources.domain: 77 atmospheric-pressure methane-based counterflow diffusion flames, 1740-2160 K.
sources.supports: Nitrogen quenching differs by a factor of three from an earlier extrapolated correlation; water is important too.
sources.doesNotSupport: Using a universal quantum yield or extrapolating a coefficient to all cold/engine conditions.
sources.implementationStatus: Numerical cross-section formula not adopted because its units and full applicability were not independently inspected in the full paper.

sources.title: C2 Swan band laser-induced fluorescence and chemiluminescence in low-pressure hydrocarbon flames
sources.reviewed: Publisher abstract and indexed paper sections
sources.domain: Low-pressure methane, ethane and ethylene premixed flames.
sources.supports: Measured fluorescence loss and absolute emission must be combined with ground-state kinetics to infer production.
sources.doesNotSupport: Equally weighted Swan bands or a universal F135 excited-state abundance.

sources.title: Line strengths and updated molecular constants for the C2 Swan system
sources.reviewed: Author preprint metadata/abstract and author software example
sources.supports: Available measured/modelled line positions and Einstein A coefficients can replace arbitrary equal band energies in an offline spectral basis.
sources.doesNotSupport: The upper-state rotational/vibrational populations, absolute F135 source power or CH-to-C2 ratio.
sources.implementationStatus: Line list not downloaded or baked in this audit; per-population spectrum needs an explicit level-population model and data license/provenance.

sources.title: Optical and probe determination of soot concentrations in a model gas turbine combustor
sources.reviewed: NASA-indexed report abstract; direct page open returned 403
sources.domain: Generic 12.7 cm combustor; four fuels, three fuel-air ratios.
sources.supports: Soot loading, particle optical properties and luminous radiation were separately measured; secondary-zone oxidation depends strongly on temperature.
sources.doesNotSupport: This F135 opacity, spatial loading, particle temperature or AB-state multiplier.

sources.title: Direct Measurement of Aircraft Engine Soot Emissions Using a Cavity-Attenuated Phase Shift (CAPS)-Based Extinction Monitor
sources.domain: V2527 high-bypass turbofan at 40-80 m downstream; about 630 nm optics.
sources.supports: Measured idle soot emission index 225±35 mg/kg and scattering albedo 0.05±0.02, with distribution peaking near 60 nm mobility diameter.
sources.doesNotSupport: Copying an idle civil-engine measurement into F135 exit soot mass, optical depth or hot particle temperature.

sources.title: Candle flame soot sizing by planar time-resolved laser-induced incandescence
sources.reviewed: Primary study results and thermal-model methods
sources.domain: Laser-heated soot in a candle flame; modeled primary diameters 1-105 nm.
sources.supports: Particle temperature is governed by a size-dependent heat balance; measured/modelled cooling is on nanosecond to microsecond scales under these conditions.
sources.doesNotSupport: An F135 particle cooling time or a long-lived hotter-than-gas reservoir without size, heating and transfer inputs.

sources.title: Afterburning Jet Thrust

sources.supports: Augmentor fuel burns in the engine aft duct before the nozzle.
